pm_exper_user_4868_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How can I cope with feeling discouraged when efforts I believed in don’t work out?
pm_exper_user_4868_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) It’s natural to feel discouraged when something you’ve worked hard on doesn’t succeed, especially after putting in so much thought and effort. You might find it grounding to revisit the core motivation behind your work, and to connect with supportive people who understand your goals. Taking time for restorative activities you enjoy can also help you reset before approaching the challenge from a fresh perspective.
(b) It’s natural to feel discouraged when climate proposals you’ve championed don’t advance, especially after investing so much evidence-based work and collaborative effort. You might find it grounding to revisit the long-term vision that drives your policy work, and to seek renewal in conversations with trusted colleagues who share your sustainability values. Taking time for restorative activities—like your weekend hiking or calligraphy—can also help you reset before approaching the challenge from a fresh angle.
(c) It’s natural to feel discouraged when Asian-American cultural heritage projects you’ve supported fail to move forward, especially after investing so much evidence-based work and collaborative effort. You might find it grounding to revisit the long-term vision that drives your advocacy, and to seek renewal in conversations with other heritage community members. Taking time for restorative activities—like your weekend hiking or calligraphy—can also help you reset before approaching the challenge from a fresh angle.
(d) It’s natural to feel discouraged when your neighborhood community garden initiatives don’t gain traction, especially after investing so much evidence-based work and collaborative effort. You might find it grounding to revisit the long-term vision that drives your local engagement, and to seek renewal in conversations with fellow volunteers who share your passion. Taking time for restorative activities—like your weekend hiking or calligraphy—can also help you reset before approaching the challenge from a fresh angle.
